# Capacity analysis (generated by analysis/capacity.py)

Analytic estimate, not a simulation result. 802.11g ERP-OFDM timing is approximate and utilization ignores collisions and retries, so real saturation starts earlier than shown. Calibrated INET 4.7.0 `requiredExchangeTime` values are 260/200 us (54 Mbps) and 820/550 us (12 Mbps).

Assumed traffic: state 1000 B at 10 Hz per AMR (uplink); orders 600 B at 5 Hz per AMR (downlink, shares the same medium); 4 stations send 200 B DDS at 100 Hz and 1400 B telemetry over the wire (Option 7B).

## 1. Airtime per successful exchange

| PHY rate | ACK rate | State exchange, CSMA (us) | Order exchange, CSMA (us) | State exchange, scheduled cw=0 (us) | Order exchange, scheduled cw=0 (us) | Max state packets/s (CSMA) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 54 Mbps | 24 Mbps | 326 | 266 | 258 | 198 | 3072 |
| 24 Mbps | 24 Mbps | 521 | 390 | 454 | 322 | 1918 |
| 12 Mbps | 12 Mbps | 882 | 618 | 814 | 550 | 1134 |
| 6 Mbps | 6 Mbps | 1606 | 1074 | 1538 | 1006 | 623 |

CSMA exchange includes DIFS, the mean backoff (CWmin/2 slots), preamble, data, SIFS and ACK. The scheduled columns have zero backoff (DATA + SIFS + ACK + DIFS). Add a safety margin when choosing `slotDuration` (400/400 us at 54 Mbps; 850/560 us at 12 Mbps).

## 3. Fleet size that reaches a target utilization

| Target | 54 Mbps | 24 Mbps | 12 Mbps | 6 Mbps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10% | 22 | 14 | 8 | 5 |
| 30% | 65 | 42 | 25 | 14 |
| 60% | 131 | 84 | 50 | 28 |
| 90% | 196 | 126 | 76 | 42 |

Reading: with the locked VDA 5050 rates (Q6), a 54 Mbps cell stays lightly loaded for the 5-40 AMR range (18% at N=40, 37% at N=80). Including the 12 Mbps PHY factor and N=80 fleet level (Q5, Q8) drives wireless utilization to 95%, exposing CSMA contention.

## 4. Wired offered load on the switch-to-FMS port (100 Mbps)

| N (AMRs) | State (Mbps) | DDS (Mbps) | + telemetry 2000 us (22.4 Mbps) | + telemetry 600 us (74.7 Mbps) | + telemetry 300 us (149.3 Mbps) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.4 | 0.86 | 24.8 | 79.7 | 158.1 |
| 10 | 0.9 | 0.86 | 25.2 | 80.1 | 158.5 |
| 20 | 1.7 | 0.86 | 26.1 | 81.0 | 159.4 |
| 40 | 3.4 | 0.86 | 27.8 | 82.7 | 161.1 |
| 80 | 6.8 | 0.86 | 31.2 | 86.1 | 164.5 |
| 120 | 10.3 | 0.86 | 34.7 | 89.5 | 167.9 |
| 200 | 17.1 | 0.86 | 41.5 | 96.4 | 174.8 |

Values include headers and the 12 B gap. Under TAS, telemetry fits 4 frames per 500 us window, a payload ceiling of about 44.8 Mbps, so TAS cells throttle telemetry by design while FIFO carries it up to link saturation.

Orders on the switch-to-AP port: N=5: 0.13 Mbps, N=10: 0.27 Mbps, N=20: 0.53 Mbps, N=40: 1.07 Mbps, N=80: 2.13 Mbps, N=120: 3.20 Mbps, N=200: 5.33 Mbps. With the locked 1 ms GCL the orders window carries at most 1 frame per 1 ms cycle (1000 orders/s), so check it against N x 5 orders/s.
